summary: Declarative, import-safe capability data for the expression backends. Under polars/, ibis/ and narwhals/ each tree has a family/ scope (FamilyWide) and dialects/<dialect>/ scopes (ibis-duckdb, ibis-sqlite, ibis-postgres, ibis-polars, ibis-mysql, ibis-singlestoredb, ibis-exasol; narwhals-polars, -pandas, -pyarrow, -duckdb, -dask, -lazy; polars). Leaf modules under substrait/ and extensions_mountainash/ each export a SEGMENT (a CapabilitySegment of CapabilityInformation and CapabilityPolicyRule records) for one domain such as string, datetime, arithmetic, list or window. core.capabilities.bootstrap discovers and binds them to their enclosing _scope.py SCOPE; the modules contain no registration side effects.
key_classes: SEGMENT (module-level CapabilitySegment) — exported by each leaf; carries domain, information and policy records
extension_points: Add a new SEGMENT leaf under <family>/<scope>/{substrait,extensions_mountainash}/<domain>.py; bootstrap.discover_declaration_modules walks the package and picks it up automatically
Add a new dialect: create dialects/<name>/_scope.py with SCOPE and register the name in core.capabilities.identity.KNOWN_DIALECTS
Underscore-prefixed modules and package __init__ files are not treated as declaration leaves
Executable behavior is expressed through CapabilityPolicyRule (consumer, action, applicability); descriptive limits through CapabilityInformation
lifecycle_notes: Declarations are scope-owned: dialect-specific limits live in the dialect tree, shared ones in family/ (see capability-as-call-property and capability-roles principles; the latter is PROPOSED, with delivered parts from PR #241)
Recent: d29e5fe0 Narwhals window-shape refusals (364, 368); 07c52c06 multi-key window refusal on pandas 3.1.0; 1344c0d7 narwhals-pandas float ranks (367); 1e4166f5 PostgreSQL Decimal gate (#396)
Segments may be retained with captured addresses so historical evidence and assertion changes survive refactors
documentation_hooks: Backend support matrix per operation and dialect (generated expression coverage report: core.capabilities.render_markdown)
How to declare a known limitation for a backend/dialect
Authoring guide for capability segments (scope, domain, information vs policy)
Known divergences page fed from these declarations
examples: Segment leaf: ibis/dialects/ibis_duckdb/substrait/string.py exports SEGMENT = CapabilitySegment(domain=Domain.STRING, information=(CapabilityInformation(key=CapabilityKey(operation=FKEY_..., subject=..., selector=Selector(...)), level=..., message=..., layer=..., applicability=unbounded),...))
Scope file: polars/family/_scope.py defines SCOPE = Scope(backend=CONST_BACKEND.POLARS, applicability=FamilyWide())
risks: Large, mostly data modules: easy to mis-scope a limit as family-wide when it is dialect-specific
A descriptive record never gates execution; only CapabilityPolicyRule records do, so documenting a limit does not prevent the call
Registration is validated per batch: unknown operation keys, params or dialects raise ValueError at load
Volume (~19k lines) means review relies on integrity and coverage tests rather than reading

evidence.detail: Docstring: import-safe scope-owned segments; every non-helper leaf exports SEGMENT, directory exports SCOPE from _scope.py
KNOWN_DIALECTS lists valid ibis-* and narwhals-* dialect names; capability-as-call-property principle
